details.description: Stable Image Style Guide is an image model from Stability AI that generates a new image following a text prompt while matching the visual style of a reference image supplied as input, rather than editing the input image's own content. Amazon Bedrock's sample request pairs a reference image with a prompt such as 'wide shot of modern metropolis' to produce a new scene rendered in that reference's style. Amazon Bedrock lists a model launch date of October 2024 for this model. Amazon Bedrock lists the model's lifecycle as Active with no confirmed end-of-life date, though its originally stated 'no sooner than' retirement window of October 2025 has passed.
advantages: Takes a reference image plus a separate text prompt to steer a newly generated image's visual style, per AWS Bedrock's sample request body.
disadvantages: Generates a new image guided by a style reference rather than directly editing the pixels of the input image, unlike Stability AI's other Stable Image edit models.
use_cases: Applying the visual style of a reference image to a newly generated scene.
Keeping brand or campaign imagery visually consistent across new generated content.
Style-guided concept art or creative exploration from a reference image.

notes: Stability AI's Sept 18, 2025 announcement of its Image Services on Amazon Bedrock names 'Style Guide' as one of its Control-category tools, alongside Style Transfer, Structure and Sketch, confirming this is Stability's own current name for the model rather than a Bedrock-only rename, so website_url now points to that announcement. Stability's general Stable Image product page (stability.ai/stable-image) still uses a shorter 'Style' label under Control rather than this full name, and platform.stability.ai's interactive API reference is a JavaScript app that could not be fetched directly to check further. Bedrock's model card lists lifecycle as Active with EOL date N/A, even though the model's originally stated 'no sooner than' end-of-life window (Oct 2025) has already passed; no source states it is deprecated or superseded.
